 Reaction as Norris wins chaotic Sao Paulo GP and Mercedes secure constructors' title
 8 November 2026 Live Reporting (active) 
 Leaderboard 
 Summary
 Lando Norris wins Sao Paulo Grand Prix
 Max Verstappen second from 21st on grid and Isack Hadjar third
 George Russell fourth after spinning in pit lane 
 Kimi Antonelli fifth after spinning off from lead 
 Mercedes win constructors' title
 Select 'listen live' for BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra commentary (UK only)
 Close form Send us your F1 views
 Get involved Live Reporting
 Lorraine McKenna
 Report: Norris wins gripping race after Antonelli and Russell errors published at 19:59 GMT 19:59 GMT 
 Andrew Benson 
BBC F1 correspondent 
 Image source, PA Media McLaren's Lando Norris beat Max Verstappen to win a gripping Sao Paulo Grand Prix in which new world champion Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes team-mate George Russell both made critical mistakes in difficult conditions. 
 Norris, who started from pole, lost the lead to Antonelli at the start and dropped back when the track was wet.
 But an earlier pit stop for dry-weather tyres put Norris on Antonelli's tail and the Italian spun away the lead at the first corner.
 After reclaiming the lead, Norris dominated through a late shower of rain which required a switch back to wet-weather tyres to take his first win since the Dutch Grand Prix at the end of August.
 A few laps before Antonelli lost the lead, Russell, who started seventh, spun exiting the pits and lost 15 to 20 seconds after working his way back into podium contention.
 Despite their travails, Russell and Antonelli finished fourth and fifth to clinch the constructors' championship for Mercedes a week after the Italian had tied up the drivers' title.
 Read the full report here 
 15 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Goodbye published at 19:58 GMT 19:58 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Choose which shindig we want to go to: Lando Norris' Sao Paulo Grand Prix victory or Mercedes' constructors' championship celebration? 
 Brazil is the perfect location for an all-night party, and with this being the third race in this latest triple-header, McLaren and the Silver Arrows crew can rejoice long into Monday morning. 
 And a double podium for Red Bull too. Max Verstappen roared from the back of the grid to finish second while team-mate Isack Hadjar came from fifth to grab third spot and his third podium of the year. 
 Is that the last we'll see of the rain this season? Probably. But Interlagos signs off having treated us to a great, if slightly chaotic, grand prix. 
 Image source, Getty Images So, we're down to the final three races of the 2026 campaign. We're definitely going back to the United States for the Las Vegas Grand Prix in two weeks' time, from 20-22 November. And as it stands, Qatar and the finale in Abu Dhabi will be following straight after. 
 Thanks for joining us for the last three weekends, folks. Enjoy a free one next week, and then come and join us at 00:30 GMT for first practice in Vegas on Friday, 20 November, 
 See you soon!

 'It was a tough weekend' - Hamilton published at 19:53 GMT 19:53 GMT 
 Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton speaking to Sky Sports after finishing ninth in Sao Paulo: "It was a really tough day and weekend for the whole team but they have done a really great job. All the mechanics did such a great job, switching out the engine, making sure the car was as good as it could be. 
 "We struggled in the dry but had a great start but unfortunately the rear tyre just ballooned and overheated and I struggled and then after that I was pushing to get on the slicks which I eventually got on, I think one of the earlier ones. I was feeling pretty good, it was very tricky in those conditions and then we ended up having an extra stop which I think ultimately, I had a lot of ground to cover from there and then just at the end, the last message I got was that it was going to stay at the drizzle and I thought 'OK, this is my moment to keep pushing because I could stay in those conditions.'
 "I didn't hear it was raining more in the first sector and I passed the pit lane and got to Turn One and it was wet so that unfortunately lost us a couple of places but otherwise, the team did a great job." 
 23 14 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 McLaren 'still need more' - Norris published at 19:49 GMT 19:49 GMT 
 McLaren's Lando Norris speaking to Sky Sports: "A day like today you've just got to try to stay in the race for as long as possible. 
 "On pure pace, I wasn't expecting a lot, I knew we had a good car today but it was clear that, on the inters especially, the Mercedes' were very quick and a little bit too quick for me. It's not all about that, especially on a day like today, you need to be consistent, you need to not make mistakes, you need to get on the right tyre at the right time - which I feel like we did a very good job of today. 
 "It was very tough, not the best first lap but when I had the opportunity to put Kimi [Antonelli] under pressure on the slicks, box him one lap earlier, give myself a chance to attack him. Part of it is he has to push and obviously he made a mistake and I could capitalise on that."
 On if McLaren end the season strongly: "I just want to win very badly. I want to be able to have a car we can fight for world championships with which we've not had throughout this year. There's been certain moments where I would say we had a car where we could fight for wins with and we did it today, we did it in a few other races this season but it's not good enough, you need a car that can fight through a whole year and you need a consistent car, you need one where you can deliver week after week. That's something we're still working on."
 14 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Feeling a bit more like myself again' - Russell published at 19:45 GMT 19:45 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Mercedes' George Russell who finished fourth at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, speaking to Sky Sports: "Yeah I am not too sure what happened [on his spin in the pit lane]. I couldn't do the full 360, I had no boost, just some of the quirks on this power unit but the main thing for today is that we got the constructors' championship. Huge amount of work from all of the team to achieve that. Obviously we would have all liked to have done it in a bit more style but we got over the line which was the most important."
 On whether things are coming together for him: "I had really strong pace in the race, especially on the soft tyre. We both struggled on the intermediate at the end, that was quite strange but feeling a bit more like myself again but this weekend I think there was definitely pure pace in there, last weekend in Mexico it was just one lap at the right time, but looking forward to Vegas."
 19 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Incredible year by everyone' - Antonelli published at 19:41 GMT 19:41 GMT 
 Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli speaking to Sky Sports about his team winning the constructors' championship: "They all deserve it. Incredible year by everyone. Not only all the people here at the track, but all the people back at the factory in Brackley and Brixworth. They've done an incredible year. 
 "It's an amazing group of people who push everyday to do their best and give us the best opportunity to fight for wins and championships. This year they've done an incredible job and that's why they deserve this championship and now we're all going to enjoy it together."
 On what was causing his issues during the race: "We need to check something with the geometry of the car, with the rear, because I had this issue only in left corners. Especially at the high speed, it was when I was feeling the most. The rear felt very unstable, even coming into the finish line, the rear was very loose which was weird. 
 "Definitely, we need to check something in the car to see what was happening, it was a very weird feeling. When I spun, the tyres were gone, all four wheels flat-spotted, it was only when I put on the second set, we got back to pace. It was a shame."
 13 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Careful! published at 19:36 GMT 19:36 GMT 
 This was the aftermath of Lando Norris' broken champagne bottle after his trademark celebration went a bit awry. Amazing how he didn't injure his hand. 
 Away from shattered glass, the McLaren man drove a fantastic race after losing the lead to Kimi Antonelli at lights out. This is his third victory of the campaign, and he's now just five points behind fifth-placed Charles Leclerc in the drivers' championship. 
 Leclerc has got that trip to stewards along with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson, which is in about 10 minutes' time, for their late incident at Turn 12. 
 Image source, Getty Images Image source, Getty Images

 Mercedes crowned title winners published at 19:32 GMT 19:32 GMT 
 In the constructors' championship, Mercedes have sealed their ninth title with 652 points, leaving Ferrari in second, 140 points adrift. 
 Red Bull continue to lead McLaren in the fight for third, but with both teams on the podium in Brazil, the gap between the two is only 17 points.

 Russell overtakes Hamilton for P3 published at 19:27 GMT 19:27 GMT 
 The race to finish second behind title winner Kimi Antonelli is the main focus until the end of the season, and with another podium under his belt, Max Verstappen has moved 17 points clear of Mercedes' George Russell, who himself has gained a position tonight and is ahead of now fourth-placed Lewis Hamilton by one point.

 32 8 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Taken a few years to be back on top spot' - Wolff published at 19:22 GMT 19:22 GMT 
 Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff speaking after securing the constructors' championship: "It's amazing. It was a very strong beginning of the season and that got us over the line, but also these last few races have been challenging. At times today it was difficult, but overall I'm so proud of the organisation. We've taken a few years to be back on the top spot, not many teams have been able to come back from that situation. It just shows the great work, the great people in our organisation and it's fantastic to be among them."
 On what it means to lead Mercedes to nine constructors' titles, equalling the record of Williams' Frank Williams: "Frank is such an unbelievable icon of the sport and to be tied on championships, I never thought that was ever possible. I had a close relationship with Frank and to be there, it's amazing. I can't believe it. There is also some of our people that have won more than nine that have been with Brawn, winning it with Honda. I take it, it's great."
 35 12 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'I could have avoided a little awkward situation with Max' - Hadjar published at 19:17 GMT 19:17 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Red Bull's Isack Hadjar who finished the race in third: "It was so, so difficult, so challenging. Especially switching from the inters to the soft tyre, avoiding the traps.
 "It was extremely difficult, especially in the pit lane you saw how tricky it was to drive. And then more rain at the end. 
 "Happy to be standing in third today but I need to keep making a bit less mistakes because I could have avoided a little awkward situation with Max, so just want to apologise because on that stint I could have kept it more on the track.
 "It was so hard because [Kimi Antonelli] was behind me and I was testing the grip for him basically. I could see he was challenging me a lot. I was on ice and he was on ice as well. It was well managed, I nearly shunted into my pit crew when boxing. But they did a fantastic job, they kept their calm and the pit stop was fast. Big thanks to the boys."
 62 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Starting P21 and being on the podium in second is a very good result' - Verstappen published at 19:13 GMT 19:13 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Red Bull's Max Verstappen speaking after gaining 19 places to finish P2 at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix: "It was a challenging race. I think the first few laps were very important, I overtook a lot of cars. 
 "Actually, that first stint on the inters was really strong. Unfortunately after that, I don't know if we picked up some kind of damage because the car felt like completely opposite to anything I've felt the whole weekend, with some really weird balance. 
 "Unfortunately, once I got into P2, I couldn't really make any inroads. We have to understand what went wrong there but starting P21 and being on the podium in second is a very good result."
 149 24 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'I kept it cool and did not make any mistakes' - Norris published at 19:09 GMT 19:09 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images McLaren's Lando Norris who has won the Sao Paulo Grand Prix from pole position: "It was a very tough race, very, very tough. Not the best of launches off the line, but a lot of challenges today with the conditions and going on slicks in the wet is always tough. Especially when you are pushing for the lead and trying to catch up a little bit so the main thing today was that I just kept it cool and I did not make any mistakes. I had the pace when I needed to so it was good. Nice to be back on the top step and what a place to do it as well."
 On how confident he was that he could get the lead back in the race: " I'm trying my best. I think this weekend we had an opportunity to get pole yesterday, an opportunity to win and I feel like most times this year when there's been an opportunity, I've went for it and we've been able to achieve it.
 "I have to say a big thanks to the team because they are still working very hard. It's annoying when you can't give them a good result back, like the last few weeks, but certainly this weekend I feel like we have been able to give something back to to them and give them a reward for their hard work. Always a big thanks to them and we will have to keep pushing until the end of the year."
 88 14 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Champions Mercedes take to the podium published at 19:06 GMT 19:06 GMT 
 Now that the top three have had their moment, it's time for Mercedes to soak up their second title celebration in two races. 
 The whole team cram onto the podium with boss Toto Wolff, drivers' world champion Kimi Antonelli and George Russell. This is Silver Arrows' first trophy since 2021, and they're loving every minute of it. 
 105 19 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Champagne moment published at 19:02 GMT 19:02 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images The national anthems are played out at Interlagos and Lando Norris takes in the applause from his McLaren team and his dad below. Is he going to do his trademark champagne bottle bang in the rain? 
 He is, but the glass bottle smashes all over the podium! Norris is left holding just the neck with a shocked look on his face. I hope he's not injured. 
 89 30 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:58 GMT 18:58 GMT 
 This is Mercedes' ninth constructors' championship, drawing them level with Williams in the all-time title winners list. 
 While the celebrations get under way in the garage and the pit lane, the top three have reached the cooldown room. Isack Hadjar opts to kneel behnd Lando Norris and Max Verstappen and watch the race highlights from behind the couch. 
 Verstappen and Norris comment that they were expecting a few nervy moments when the slick tyres came out, but in the end, we lost only Lance Stroll during the race with a reliability issue (Valtteri Bottas failed to start).

 Being a Hamilton fan is painful, to say the least. Pretty shocking all around, yet again...

 189 47 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Norris wins in Sao Paulo published at 18:52 GMT 18:52 GMT 
 Behind the top five, Oscar Piastri ends his time in Brazil in sixth place, ahead of the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc and the Racing Bulls of Liam Lawson, however, the battle between Leclerc and Lawson is going to be investigated after the race, as the pair made contact at Turn 12. 
 Lewis Hamilton comes from P20 to finish in ninth place, while Audi's Nico Hulkenberg takes the final points place in 10th. 
 99 23 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:49 GMT 18:49 GMT 
 Sam Bird 
Former Formula E driver on 5 Sports Extra 
 Masterclass from Lando Norris, proving why he is a world champion. OK, he's not won it this year but what a drive from him, in tricky conditions, changing conditions and Max Verstappen coming home in P2 from the back of the grid. And congratulations to Mercedes, on yet another constructors' world championship.

 Team radio - McLaren to Norris published at 18:46 GMT 18:46 GMT 
 Engineer: "Well done mate."
 Norris: "Woohoo! Nicely done! Well done guys, you all deserve it. You keep working hard, I try to deliver and today we did. Credit to you all. Let's keep it going."
